recovered_entries.endogenous_note: Added because it is the reference case for what NONE actually means, and because the antioxidant-during-chemotherapy entry leaned on it without naming the reason. Humans carry a non-functional pseudogene for L-gulonolactone oxidase (GULO), the last enzyme of ascorbate synthesis, so synthesis is zero and the loss is genetic, not dietary (PMID 8175804). Most mammals make their own; we do not. This is the opposite situation to the NAD intermediates: here the endogenous axis argues for intake, a deficiency disease exists with a defined clinical picture, and the supplement genuinely fills a gap when intake is low.

recovered_entries.endogenous_note: Vitamin C is the paradigm case of NONE arising from a lost pathway rather than from being an element. Humans carry the terminal enzyme L-gulonolactone oxidase only as a non-functional pseudogene (GULOP), which is why we develop scurvy while rats and dogs, which retain GULO, do not. Every milligram of ascorbate is dietary, so supplementation is never redundant on this axis and is justified purely by intake, losses and the plateau of tissue saturation.

recovered_entries.supplement: Vitamin D (cholecalciferol) as a standalone supplement
recovered_entries.endogenous_note: This is the strongest FULL case in nutrition and the one that tests the redundancy claim directly. Skin makes cholecalciferol from 7-dehydrocholesterol whenever UVB reaches it, and exposure alone can meet requirement without any toxicity risk, because previtamin D3 photodegrades to lumisterol and tachysterol and CYP24A1 clears the active hormone. So the supplement is genuinely redundant for someone with regular summer sun on bare skin, and genuinely necessary when UVB is absent. The verdict depends on exposure rather than on biochemistry, which is why blanket claims in either direction are wrong.

recovered_entries.endogenous: PARTIAL, as conversion of dietary vitamin K rather than de novo synthesis; NONE for the naphthoquinone ring itself
recovered_entries.endogenous_note: MK-4 is routinely misrepresented in supplement marketing. Humans cannot make the naphthoquinone ring, so vitamin K itself is entirely dietary, but UBIAD1 prenylates menadione derived from dietary phylloquinone (K1) to MK-4 in most tissues, so the specific form sold as K2 MK-4 is one the body already produces from ordinary K1 intake. Supplementing MK-4 duplicates that conversion. The honest arguments for a K2 product are pharmacokinetic, since MK-7 has a much longer half-life than K1, and dietary, for people eating little natto, cheese or leafy greens.

recovered_entries.endogenous_note: CLA is usually presented as purely dietary, and it has a real partial human route: trans-vaccenic acid from ruminant fat is desaturated to c9,t11-CLA by stearoyl-CoA desaturase (SCD1) in human tissue. The t10,c12 isomer that dominates commercial supplements and drives the claimed fat-loss effect has no human synthetic route at all, so the isomer sold differs from the one human tissue forms, and the weight-loss category is not uniformly NONE as originally claimed.

recovered_entries.endogenous_note: Humans convert dietary phylloquinone (K1) and menadione to menaquinone-4 in tissue using UBIAD1, which prenylates the menadione ring, so the MK-4 in artery wall, bone and brain is partly endogenous even though the quinone ring itself is strictly dietary and cannot be synthesised. Colonic bacteria make long-chain menaquinones from MK-7 to MK-13, and their contribution to human vitamin K status is modest and hard to quantify because much of it stays unabsorbed in the colon. That combination is what makes vitamin K a real PARTIAL: the ring cannot be made, the specific K2 form largely can, given K1 in the diet.

The vitamin requirement exists because that de novo route is limited, runs essentially only in liver, and starts from tryptophan, which is itself dietary. recovered_entries.endogenous_note: Niacin is the case in this set with a real conversion ratio to compute. The body makes niacin equivalents from tryptophan along the kynurenine pathway at roughly 60 mg tryptophan per 1 mg niacin equivalent, so 1 g of dietary tryptophan yields about 16.7 mg NE, close to the 16 mg NE/day RDA for men. Conversion needs riboflavin, vitamin B6 and iron for the pathway enzymes, which is why pellagra appears where maize-based diets bind niacin and protein quality is poor, and in Hartnup disease and carcinoid where tryptophan is lost or diverted.

recovered_entries.endogenous_note: Four labels are used, and adequate quantity is judged against basal physiological function at the tissue's normal set point, not against a storage ceiling and not against the dose a trial happened to use. FULL: the human pathway is complete and output covers basal need in health. PARTIAL: the pathway exists but output is structurally capped below what the relevant pool or function needs, so dietary supply routinely contributes. recovered_entries.endogenous_note_zh: 全表用四个标签, 判断供应是否充足的基准是健康状态下组织在正常设定点的基础生理功能, 不按储存池上限, 也不按某项试验所用剂量。FULL: 人体通路完整, 健康时自身产量覆盖基础需要。PARTIAL: 通路存在, 但产量在结构上被限制在相关池或功能所需之下, 饮食供应经常性参与。CONDITIONAL: 健康时够用, 在明确点名的状态下不够用。NONE: 人体完全没有该生物合成通路, 所有化学元素都归此类, 因为没有生物能合成元素。标签是描述性的: NONE 不含需求含义 (caffeine 和 quercetin 是 NONE 且无需求, vitamin C 和 zinc 是 NONE 但有需求也有缺乏症), FULL 也不能判定药理剂量是否有效 (melatonin 即是)。

recovered_entries.still_matters_when: Use the axis to decide whether a product has a target, then use pharmacology and trial evidence to decide whether it works. The axis can kill a premise (glucosamine, collagen as a molecule, test boosters) and it can support one (creatine, beta-alanine, vitamin C at low intake, B12 in a vegan). It never settles efficacy on its own.
recovered_entries.still_matters_when_zh: 先用这条轴判断产品有没有可作用的目标, 再用药理学和试验证据判断它是否有效。这条轴能否掉某些前提 (glucosamine, 作为分子的 collagen, 睾酮增强类产品), 也能支持某些前提 (creatine, beta-alanine, 摄入不足时的 vitamin C, 纯素者的 B12), 但它本身从不判定疗效。
